curated.background:
Source. Erdős Problem 307 in the Erdős problems database; the page says the question was asked by Barbeau: https://www.erdosproblems.com/307

Known partial results. According to the problem page, $P$ and $Q$ must be disjoint and the reciprocals of the primes in $P \cup Q$ must sum to at least $2$, so $P \cup Q$ has at least $60$ elements. If the elements are only required to be pairwise coprime and $1$ is allowed as an element, examples exist, such as $(1 + \tfrac{1}{5})(\tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{1}{3}) = 1$.

Status record. The status database linked from the problem page is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml . There the state verifiable means open and resolvable by a finite example.

lean_target.correspondence: P and Q are finite sets of natural numbers all of whose elements are prime. The reciprocals are taken in the rational numbers, and the proposition asks that the product of the two sums of reciprocals equals 1. As in the statement, the two sets are not required to be disjoint or different.
lean_target.text:
import Mathlib

def wishpool_target_prop : Prop :=
  ∃ P Q : Finset ℕ, (∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) ∧ (∀ q ∈ Q, q.Prime) ∧
    (∑ p ∈ P, (1 : ℚ) / (p : ℚ)) * (∑ q ∈ Q, (1 : ℚ) / (q : ℚ)) = 1

curated.name: Barbeau's question on two finite sets of primes with reciprocal sums multiplying to 1 (Erdős Problem 307)
curated.source_license: Licence of the source not determined on 2026-11-11; the statement is restated in the curator's own words.
curated.statement:
Question. Do there exist two finite sets of primes $P$ and $Q$ such that

$$\Bigl( \sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} \Bigr) \Bigl( \sum_{q \in Q} \frac{1}{q} \Bigr) = 1\,?$$
